jobs.title: Senior Vice President, Enterprise Risk Management
jobs.description:
Experience Aviva

Together, we are Aviva.

Our values of Care, Commitment, Community, and Confidence guide how we show up for each other and our customers. At Aviva Canada, we put people first through a culture built on inclusion, collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement.

The Opportunity

The SVP, Enterprise Risk Management is a key member of the Aviva Canada Senior Risk Leadership Team, responsible for providing enterprise-wide leadership across risk business partnering, quantitative risk, insurance and financial risk, capital, model risk, and risk analytics. The role supports the effective performance of Aviva Canada by overseeing the implementation of the Risk Management Framework, providing independent oversight and challenge to the first line, and ensuring the organization operates within its Board-approved risk appetite.

Working closely with the Chief Risk Officer, Executive Committee, and business leaders, the SVP delivers commercially focused risk insight and independent challenge on strategic and business decisions. The role acts as a trusted advisor to senior stakeholders, ensuring robust governance, effective risk management, and a strong risk culture that support Aviva Canada's strategic objectives, regulatory obligations, and long-term resilience.

What You'll Do

In this role, you will be accountable for the following key areas:

Enterprise Risk Leadership and Strategy

Partner with the ACAN CRO to shape and execute Aviva Canada's risk strategy and ensure the effective operation of the Risk Management Framework.
Provide independent, commercially focused risk insight and challenge to support strategic decision-making, growth objectives, and long-term value creation.
Ensure the organization operates within Board-approved risk appetite and maintains effective risk governance, oversight, and risk culture.
Support Executive Committee, Board Risk Committee, and ACAN Board reporting on key risk exposures, emerging risks, and risk management effectiveness.

Risk Oversight and Independent Challenge

Lead independent oversight of Aviva Canada's aggregate risk profile, including insurance, financial, capital, model, technology, data, change, and operational risks.
Provide effective review and challenge of business plans, capital deployment decisions, reinsurance strategies, material transactions, product development, pricing, and other significant business initiatives.
Monitor emerging risks and material changes in risk exposure, ensuring appropriate mitigation strategies are identified and executed.
Escalate significant risk issues and risk appetite breaches, providing clear recommendations for remediation and management action.

Quantitative, Capital and Model Risk Management

Provide enterprise leadership for insurance risk, financial risk, capital risk, risk modelling and risk analytics.
Accountable for overseeing Internal Model Independent Validation (IMIV) and material model governance across Aviva Canada.
Oversee independent validation activities and provide challenge on capital adequacy, economic capital, liquidity, financial resilience, and risk-return optimization.
Drive the evolution of quantitative risk capabilities and risk analytics to enhance business decision making and risk insights.

Business Partnering and Stakeholder Management

Lead the Risk Business Partnering team, ensuring Risk is a trusted advisor and constructive challenger to business leaders across Aviva Canada.
Build strong relationships with EC, regulators, Board members, Group Risk teams, and external stakeholders
Represent Risk on key governance committees, industry forums, and global initiatives, promoting effective risk management practices and influencing outcomes.
Foster a culture of transparency, collaboration, and proactive risk management across the organization.

People Leadership and Functional Excellence

Lead and develop a high-performing team across Risk Business Partnering and Quantitative Risk.
Establish clear priorities, performance expectations, and accountability for delivery of high-quality risk outcomes.
Build organizational capability in risk management, business partnering, analytics, and technical risk disciplines.
Promote a culture of continuous improvement, talent development, and succession planning while ensuring Risk operates as a cohesive and high-performing function.

What You'll Bring

Bachelor’s degree and relevant professional designation (e.g., FCAS, FCIA, FSA, CRM) or equivalent combination of education and experience.
15+ years of progressive risk leadership experience within the insurance and/or broader financial services industry.
Deep expertise in Enterprise Risk Management, including risk governance, risk appetite, risk culture, ORSA, stress testing, capital management, and regulatory compliance.
Strong understanding of insurance risks, including underwriting, pricing, claims, reserving, reinsurance, investments, and emerging risks.
Experience engaging with Boards, Board Risk Committees, and regulators (OSFI and/or equivalent regulatory bodies).
Proven ability to develop and execute risk strategies that support business objectives, customer outcomes, and sustainable growth.
Exceptional leadership and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to build high-performing teams and influence executives, regulators, and cross-functional partners.
Strong strategic, analytical, and communication capabilities, including the ability to translate complex risk, actuarial, and financial information into clear business insights and drive organizational change.

What You'll Get

Competitive executive compensation package, including annual incentive opportunities.
Comprehensive pension and retirement savings programs.
Flexible hybrid work model.
Industry-leading health and wellness benefits.
Professional development and executive leadership growth opportunities.
Inclusive employee resource groups and diversity initiatives.
Volunteer opportunities and community impact programs.
Competitive vacation and wellness offerings.

jobs.title: Head of Sales ZEISS Medical Technology - Ophthalmology
jobs.description:
About Us

How many companies can say they’ve been in business for over 177 years?!

Here at ZEISS, we certainly can! As the pioneers of science, ZEISS handles the everchanging environments in a fast-paced world, meeting it with cutting edge of technologies and continuous advancements. ZEISS believes that innovation and technology are the key to a sustainable future and solutions for global change. We have a diverse range of portfolios throughout the ZEISS family in segments like, Industrial Quality & Research, Medical Technology, Consumer Markets and Semiconductor Manufacturing Technology. We are a global company with over 42,000 employees and have over 4,000 in the US and Canada alone! Make a difference, come join the team!

What’s the role?

The Head of Sales ZEISS Medical Technology Ophthalmology is responsible for leading the Canadian commercial strategy, sales execution, revenue growth, profitability and market development for the Ophthalmic Devices business.

This role provides leadership across key Ophthalmic Devices segments, including ophthalmic diagnostics, surgical ophthalmology, refractive solutions, retina, anterior segment and related clinical education or professional development activities, as applicable to the Canadian market.

The incumbent is accountable for achieving annual revenue and profit objectives, developing a high-performing sales organization, strengthening customer relationships and ensuring alignment with ZEISS Canada priorities, regional business objectives and global Ophthalmic Devices strategies.

The role is also responsible for providing business insights to Canadian and regional leadership on market trends, customer needs, competitive activity, product requirements, pricing, territory planning and growth opportunities within the Canadian ophthalmology and optometry markets.

Sound Interesting?

Here’s What You’ll Do

Commercial Strategy and Business Planning

Develop and execute the Canadian Ophthalmic Devices commercial strategy in alignment with ZEISS Canada, regional and global business priorities.
Lead the achievement of annual revenue, profit and market share objectives for the Canadian Ophthalmic Devices business.
Develop annual business plans, sales forecasts, expense budgets and growth initiatives.
Provide regular business updates, sales funnel reviews and forecast submissions to Canadian and regional leadership.
Lead monthly business reviews using data-driven performance analysis
Lead capital equipment opportunity planning from lead generation through installation, customer adoption and lifecycle management.
Monitor installed base performance, replacement opportunities and cross-selling opportunities across the customer portfolio.
Recommend pricing strategies, promotional programs, territory planning, resource allocation and future product opportunities based on Canadian market needs.
Identify incremental business opportunities with strategic partners, key accounts and healthcare institutions.

Sales Leadership and Performance Management

Lead the Canadian Ophthalmic Devices sales organization in achieving annual sales and profitability targets.
Build, coach and develop a high-performing sales team through effective recruitment, onboarding, motivation, mentoring and performance management.
Establish clear sales goals, territory expectations and accountability measures.
Support career development, succession planning and talent growth within the Canadian sales organization.
Operate as a player-coach by actively participating in strategic customer engagements, major sales presentations, executive-level negotiations, and key opportunity pursuits.
Conduct regular performance discussions and annual performance reviews in accordance with ZEISS Canada HR policies.
Partner with Regional Sales Managers and Account Managers to develop account strategies, advance complex opportunities, and accelerate sales cycle progression.
Conduct regular field coaching, joint customer visits, and opportunity reviews to improve sales effectiveness and support professional development across the commercial organization.
Leverage Salesforce as the primary commercial management platform and single source of truth for pipeline management, account planning, forecasting, opportunity coaching, performance management, and commercial analytics, ensuring data integrity, visibility, and sales execution across the organization.
Utilize CRM analytics to drive territory optimization, resource allocation, customer segmentation and business planning decisions.
Utilize Salesforce analytics and reporting to support territory optimization, customer segmentation, resource allocation, forecasting accuracy, and strategic business planning.
Foster a culture of collaboration, accountability, customer focus and achievement.

Market Development and Competitive Intelligence

Monitor and evaluate Canadian market trends, customer needs, competitive activity, procurement practices and emerging opportunities in ophthalmology and optometry.
Provide regular and meaningful insights to Canadian and regional leadership on market conditions, customer requirements, product needs and competitive positioning.
Analyze market intelligence, customer feedback, sales data and pipeline information to identify risks and growth opportunities.
Recommend strategies to strengthen ZEISS’s market position in Canada.
Reinforce ZEISS’s brand as a trusted market leader in ophthalmic technology and solutions.

Customer and Strategic Account Management

Build and maintain strong relationships with key customers, strategic accounts, ophthalmologists, optometrists, clinics, hospitals, academic institutions and buying groups.
Lead complex sales opportunities involving Requests for Proposal (RFPs), public tenders, group purchasing organizations (GPOs), and hospital procurement processes.
Coordinate cross-functional resources including Clinical Applications, Marketing, Service, Finance, and Regulatory teams to develop competitive proposals and customer solutions.
Develop winning bid strategies and ensure timely submission of proposals aligned with customer requirements and ZEISS commercial objectives.
Monitor upcoming capital equipment procurement opportunities and healthcare funding initiatives to proactively position ZEISS solutions.
Represent ZEISS Canada at industry events, conferences, customer forums and strategic business discussions.
Partner with internal stakeholders to resolve customer issues and improve the overall customer experience.
Develop and oversee national strategic account plans for key customers, buying groups, hospital networks and academic institutions.
Establish executive engagement plans for high-value customers and strategic growth accounts.
Monitor account performance, share of wallet and customer retention metrics.
Ensure customer insights are communicated back to Marketing, Service, Finance, Clinical Education and regional leadership teams.

Marketing, Product and Commercial Excellence

Partner with Marketing and regional business leaders on product positioning, launch planning, promotional programs and market deve lopment initiatives.
Provide input into product line strategy, market penetration plans and future product requirements for Canada.
Support the implementation of sales contests, sales meetings, product launches and commercial initiatives.
Ensure effective use of CRM, pipeline management tools and sales reporting processes.
Collaborate with Clinical Education and Professional Development to support customer training, adoption and product utilization.

Financial Management and Forecasting

Manage revenue plans, expense budgets, sales forecasts and profitability objectives for the Canadian Ophthalmic Devices business.
Provide accurate and timely forecast updates to Finance, Canadian leadership and regional stakeholders.
Review monthly revenue and expense projections, customer issues, sales activity and competitive business encounters.
Maintain a rolling forecast and identify corrective actions where performance gaps arise.
Ensure business decisions are supported by sound financial analysis and commercial judgment.

Cross-Functional and Matrix Leadership

Work closely with ZEISS Canada leadership, regional Ophthalmic Devices leadership, Finance, Human Resources, Marketing, Service, Clinical Education, Regulatory/Quality and other internal stakeholders.
Contribute to Canadian leadership discussions on matters related to Ophthalmic Devices strategy, sales execution, customer experience and business performance.
Influence across a matrix environment to align priorities, resources and business outcomes.
Ensure communication of corporate goals, strategies and tactics to the Canadian sales organization.

Compliance, Quality and Policy Adherence

Maintain awareness of and adherence to applicable ZEISS policies, quality processes and regulatory requirements.
Ensure the Canadian sales organization operates in accordance with company standards, compliance expectations and ethical business practices.
Support adherence to applicable medical device quality, documentation and customer-facing processes.
Maintain a safe, respectful and professional work environment.

Do you qualify?

Experience And Education Requirements

Bachelor's degree in Business, Life Sciences, Healthcare, Engineering or related discipline.
MBA or advanced degree considered an asset.
Minimum 8-10 years of progressive medical device or healthcare sales leadership experience.
Medical device, healthcare technology or ophthalmology/optometry market experience strongly preferred.
Experience leading sales teams and achieving revenue and profitability targets.
Experience selling or leading teams that sell diagnostic, surgical, refractive or related ophthalmic products considered an asset.
Experience working in a matrix organization considered an asset.
Experience managing budgets, forecasts, sales performance and customer relationships.
Strong business acumen and financial analysis capability.
Strong understanding of sales strategy, forecasting, pipeline management and commercial execution.
Ability to analyze complex business situations and make sound recommendations.
Strong leadership, coaching and talent development skills.
Excellent presentation and executive communication skills.
Strong customer relationship management and negotiation skills.
Ability to influence across functions and organizational levels.
Strong planning, organizational and problem-solving skills.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office, CRM tools and business reporting systems.
Bilingual English/French considered an asset.

Working Conditions And Special Demands

Standard working hours are typically 40 hours per week Monday – Friday.
In some cases, especially with the advancement of technology, remote work or flexible work arrangement may be possible. This depends on company’s policies and the nature of the work.
Willing to travel over weekends and holidays, including domestic and international travel (up to 25% - 50%).
Ability to work in a multi-cultural business environment, foreign language skills are desirable.

This job description contains the general details considered necessary to outline the principal functions of the job and shall not be construed as inclusive of all work requirements. All position requirements are subject to modification to reasonably accommodate individuals with a disability. The Company reserves

The annual pay range for this position is $165,000 – $206,000 The pay offered for this role may be influenced by factors such as job location, scope of role, qualifications, education, experience, & complexity/specialization/scarcity of talent. This position is also eligible for a performance bonus or sales commissions. ZEISS also offers robust benefits, including medical plans, retirement savings plan and paid time off.

We have amazing benefits to support you as an employee at ZEISS!

jobs.title: Director, Talent & Workforce Strategy
jobs.description:
The Opportunity

Company,
Department
: Nova Scotia Power, Human Resources

Location
: Halifax, Nova Scotia

Type of Employment:
Full-time, Regular

Closing Date:
September 30th, 2026

At Nova Scotia Power
, the company's greatest source of energy has always been its people
. The organization works in every community across the province, from Yarmouth to Wreck Cove, Cape Breton. Every day, their teams are committed to providing safe, reliable electricity so that customers and communities can thrive.

Are you a forward-thinking HR leader who can connect business strategy with the people and capabilities needed to bring it to life? Nova Scotia Power is seeking a Director, Talent & Workforce Strategy to lead an integrated approach to workforce planning, talent acquisition, talent and leadership development, succession planning, diversity, equity and inclusion, and organizational effectiveness. Reporting to the Senior Director, Human Resources, this is a highly influential role with the opportunity to shape Nova Scotia Power's workforce strategy during a pivotal period of transformation.

Key Elements Of This Role Include

As the Director, Talent & Workforce Strategy,
you will develop and lead a forward-looking workforce strategy aligned with Nova Scotia Power's long-term business priorities. Working closely with senior leaders and Emera's Corporate HR team, you will anticipate future workforce and capability needs, strengthen talent and succession pathways, and create opportunities to develop and reskill employees as roles and technologies evolve. Using workforce analytics and market intelligence, you will translate emerging needs into practical strategies while building partnerships with educational institutions, industry associations, and talent networks.

The ideal candidate is a strategic and visionary HR leader who is equally comfortable seeing the big picture and translating it into action. You are an exceptional relationship builder with strong business acumen, sound judgement, and the ability to build trust and influence across a complex organization. You bring 10 or more years of progressive HR or talent management experience, including demonstrated success leading enterprise-wide talent and workforce initiatives and partnering with executive leadership. A bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Organizational Development, or a related field is required. A CPHR designation and change management certification are considered assets.

Nova Scotia Power is looking for a curious, collaborative, and future focused leader who understands the important connection between people and business strategy. This is an opportunity to help build the workforce needed to power Nova Scotia's future while contributing to an organization whose work has a meaningful impact on communities across the province every day.

To learn more about Nova Scotia Power
, please visit: https://www.nspower.ca/about-us

Please submit your resume online to www.facetconnect.com.
For more information, contact Madyson
MacIntyre
confidentially at mmacintyre@facetconnect.com. If you need accommodation during the selection process, please let us know.

Facet is a recruitment firm with an unshakeable belief that change is a good thing. People are not only our purpose, they are also our passion. Facet was created to recruit talented, established professionals who aspire to lead organizations. We are inspired by these individuals and believe they are at the core of building purpose-driven, dynamic, and forward-thinking workplaces.

Learn more about our culture and values

At the Emera Group of Companies, you’ll be part of an inclusive, respectful workplace where everyone is welcomed and supported. Come build a career as unique as you are: making an impact from Atlantic Canada to the world. Your experience and perspective will help us to safely deliver cleaner, more reliable energy to our customers.

If working in an innovative environment, challenging yourself, and shaping a cleaner energy future inspires you, we want to hear from you.

Diversity, Equity & Inclusion at Emera

As one of Atlantic Canada’s largest publicly traded companies, we are ranked one of Canada’s Top 100 Employers, Top Employers for Young People and Top Diversity Employers. We know our success is driven by our dedicated teams and we strongly encourage applications from all qualified candidates, including persons who identify as racially visible, Indigenous, persons with disabilities, women in underrepresented roles and members of the 2SLGBTQ+ community.

Applicants from these equity groups may self-identify through the online application process. We support candidates and employees with access and accommodation needs and encourage you to let us know when you require accommodation.

Recruitment & Promotion Policy

The success of the Emera Company is driven by its people: a strong team with a shared commitment to support the Emera Company mission and values. The purpose of our recruitment policy is to provide a consistent framework to support fair and equitable attraction, hiring, and retention of the best talent for vacant positions. We are dedicated to maintaining a fair hiring process that provides equitable opportunities to all our applicants and is guided by our company values.

At Nova Scotia Power
, the company's greatest source of energy has always been its people
. The organization works in every community across the province, from Yarmouth to Wreck Cove, Cape Breton. Every day, their teams are committed to providing safe, reliable electricity so that customers and communities can thrive.

Are you a forward-thinking HR leader who can connect business strategy with the people and capabilities needed to bring it to life? Nova Scotia Power is seeking a Director, Talent & Workforce Strategy to lead an integrated approach to workforce planning, talent acquisition, talent and leadership development, succession planning, diversity, equity and inclusion, and organizational effectiveness. Reporting to the Senior Director, Human Resources, this is a highly influential role with the opportunity to shape Nova Scotia Power's workforce strategy during a pivotal period of transformation.

Key Elements Of This Role Include

As the Director, Talent & Workforce Strategy,
you will develop and lead a forward-looking workforce strategy aligned with Nova Scotia Power's long-term business priorities. Working closely with senior leaders and Emera's Corporate HR team, you will anticipate future workforce and capability needs, strengthen talent and succession pathways, and create opportunities to develop and reskill employees as roles and technologies evolve. Using workforce analytics and market intelligence, you will translate emerging needs into practical strategies while building partnerships with educational institutions, industry associations, and talent networks.

The ideal candidate is a strategic and visionary HR leader who is equally comfortable seeing the big picture and translating it into action. You are an exceptional relationship builder with strong business acumen, sound judgement, and the ability to build trust and influence across a complex organization. You bring 10 or more years of progressive HR or talent management experience, including demonstrated success leading enterprise-wide talent and workforce initiatives and partnering with executive leadership. A bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Organizational Development, or a related field is required. A CPHR designation and change management certification are considered assets.

Nova Scotia Power is looking for a curious, collaborative, and future focused leader who understands the important connection between people and business strategy. This is an opportunity to help build the workforce needed to power Nova Scotia's future while contributing to an organization whose work has a meaningful impact on communities across the province every day.
